lede: Materials Project experimental entries (AB 1,139 and ABX<sub>3</sub> 790 compositions), structure type as the label, TabPFN-3.5 as the in-context engine with TabICLv2 and CatBoost as checks, five seeds. Decision rules fixed in the plan before the run.
conclusion:
No route is decided (plan 4.2: “uncertain”). The two stoichiometry classes trigger different protocol-B rules: AB triggers B1 (rule-prior PFN route) and ABX3 triggers B2 (no rule prior; more labels or a conditional generative model), and the AB call sits on its threshold: pooled repair ratio 0.50 at k = 10 (95% CI 0.48–0.53, four of five seeds below 0.5), 0.45 with L1 labels.

Within families (protocol A), a same-family context beats an other-family context by 37 pp (AB) and 19 pp (ABX3) at k = 20, but a nearest-neighbour context beats the same-family context by 14 pp and 7 pp, and no in-context condition reaches the global model. For AB this is rule A2 (the gain is locality in descriptor space); for ABX3 it cannot be read, because 89% of the nearest neighbours are already same-family.

Confidence: the protocol-A differences are large, have narrow CIs and keep their sign across both engines, both label schemes and both partitions; the protocol-B results that decide the route are fragile.
data: Entries with theoretical=False (all carry an ICSD id), one entry per composition (lowest energy_above_hull), noble gases and AB hydrides removed. L1 is the Wyckoff skeleton (space group + (multiplicity, site symmetry) per site role); L2 maps each structure to an aristotype of the reference library by framework matching, otherwise it keeps its L1 skeleton. Classes beyond the top K form other. P1 families are chemical (AB: intermetallic or the group of the more electronegative element; ABX3: the anion); P2 families are Louvain communities of the single-substitution graph. Families under 15 members were merged into the nearest centroid.
t1_caption: ABX3 needed K = 18 L1 classes to bring other to 30%; under L2 the distorted perovskites merge into one class, so K = 8 suffices. The AB P1 families are uneven: intermetallics hold half of the compositions (572 of 1,139). The Goldschmidt factor is missing for 17% of ABX3 (no oxidation-state solution or no Shannon radius); the engines take the NaN as is.
protocol_a: Each family is split 80/20 by label. C1 fits on all training rows; C2 draws k rows from the query's own family, C3 from the other families, five draws averaged; C4 takes the k training rows nearest to each query in z-scored feature space. Differences are paired over the same queries, averaged per seed; the CI is a percentile bootstrap over the five seed-level values (n = 5, so the interval is coarse).
f1_AB: C4 lies above C2 at every k and C2 never reaches the global model (dashed). C3 stays near 20%: other families rarely contain the query's class (coverage 81% at k = 20 versus 89% for C2). Hover a point for its value and CI.
f1_ABX3: The same order as AB with smaller gaps. C2 − C3 is only 3 pp at k = 5 and largest at k = 10 (24 pp). At k = 50 only 77% of the queries remain, because the smaller anion families have fewer than 50 training rows.
t3_caption: Bold blue: the difference is at least 5 pp and its 95% CI excludes 0; blue: at least 3 pp as a point estimate. The decision is read at k = 20 and needs the same sign at k = 10. C2 − C4 is negative at every k. A C4 same-family share of 0.8 or more makes C2 − C4 unreadable for H1' (plan 4.3); ABX<sub>3</sub> is above that line at every k.
protocol_b: Each family is held out in turn. C1 fits on all other families and predicts the whole held-out family; C2 uses only k rows of the held-out family and scores the remaining ones, drawing contexts until every query has at least three valid predictions. The protocol-A level is C1 on that family's protocol-A test part (an unpaired reference). The repair ratio is (C2 − C1<sub>B</sub>) / (C1<sub>A</sub> − C1<sub>B</sub>), pooled with |F| weights.
f2_AB: Holding out the intermetallics drops the global model from 78% to 14%: the other five families are ionic or covalent compounds. Ten intermetallic samples bring it back to 56%. In the other five families ten samples gain at most 10 pp and lose in two of them, so the pooled ratio of 0.50 is mostly the intermetallic family.
f2_ABX3: For most anions the global model trained on the other anions beats a ten-sample same-family context; only the fluorides gain from their own samples (55% → 71%). The pooled repair ratio is negative (−0.42, 95% CI −0.60 to −0.23). For X = Cl the protocol-A level (45%) is below the held-out level (62%); the two are scored on different samples.
checks: All sign checks pass: C2 − C3 is positive and C2 − C4 negative for both engines on the main combinations, for both label schemes and for both partitions. CatBoost stays within 5 pp of TabPFN's C1 on seven of the eight combinations; on AB × L2 × P2 TabPFN is 5.0 pp higher than CatBoost in protocol A (73.6% vs 68.6%), so the check fails narrowly; the PFN baseline is the stronger one, so the failure does not point to an engine defect. The C4 same-family share stays below 0.8 except for ABX<sub>3</sub> × P1, where neighbours of the same anion dominate.
combos_caption: Rule A follows the plan 4.2 table, with C2 − C4 treated as unreadable where the C4 same-family share is 0.8 or more. Rule B: A1–A3 and B1–B3 are the rows of that table. Protocol A gives A2 or uncertain in every combination. Protocol B gives B2 everywhere except AB × L2 × P1 (B1, with both engines) and AB × L2 × P2 (uncertain: a 9.9 pp gap, between the 5 and 10 pp thresholds).
deviations:
• TabPFN-3.5 weights downloaded from the public Hugging Face repository instead of the package's token-gated auto-download; same default checkpoint.
  • Aristotype matching capped at 60 s per comparison; two AB compositions hit the cap (BCl, MgIr) and count as unmatched for those references.
  • Single-class contexts are answered with probability 1 for that class without calling the engine.
  • The 1:1 and 1:1:3 tests use element-amount ratios, so the six alkali and hydrogen peroxides, which pymatgen does not reduce, stay in AB.
  • Reference library: four hexagonal perovskite polytypes (2H, 4H, 6H, 9R), calcite and aragonite separately; distorted perovskites match the cubic reference without extra references.
  • The L2 map was spot-checked by the analysing agent and left unchanged; it still needs a crystallographer's review. Doubtful merges include WC-type → CrB and some Pbca structures → wurtzite.
  • The first protocol-B row of the plan's 4.2 table lost its conclusion and route columns; it is read as “extrapolation fails, ≤ 10 samples repair it → rule-prior PFN route”.
  • The plan 4.3 C4 same-family rule is applied inside rule A, which makes ABX3 × P1 “uncertain” in protocol A.
  • Added, not in the plan: a seed-level bootstrap CI of the pooled repair ratio, used only to state how close AB is to the 0.5 threshold.
  • Compute: RIKYU GB200, 12 GPUs × 16 units, 19 min wall clock; per-fit timings in the experiment README.
next:
The plan's next step depends on the route, and the route is uncertain. Two observations narrow the next experiment:

  • Within families, retrieval beats family membership everywhere (C4 > C2), which points to the locality route (kNN or a generic PFN with a retrieved context). The first experiment there: C4 against C1 and against a retrieved context of the same size drawn from a larger pool, testing whether retrieval closes the gap to C1.
  • The only cross-family failure that few samples repair is the AB intermetallic family. Before building a rule prior on it, rerun protocol B with the intermetallics split by chemistry (e.g. by the group of the more electronegative metal), so that one family no longer decides the pooled ratio. Adding seeds will not move a ratio whose CI already brackets 0.5.
  • The mixed context (global data plus k same-family rows) is outside this plan; it is the condition a production model would use, and the ABX3 result (the global model beats ten own samples) makes it the obvious follow-up.
